correctness.rationale: Exact Steele–Beer depth integration and strict Jensen positivity are independently derived. A three-exponential derivative has at most two real zeros, one fixed at t=0, forcing exactly one positive density-gap maximum; a one-crossing cumulative criterion and equality boundary follow. All roots, inequalities and high-light scales hold for the explicitly stated positive parameter domain. The standalone standard-library checker passed 10,510 assertions, but the analytical proof—not finite sampling—establishes the quantified theorem.

originality.rationale: The exact two-level, arbitrarily weighted one-cutoff phase classification and large-light asymptotic were not found in the inspected primary articles or the closest full public mathematical result. The prior Steele–Beer integral is explicitly not claimed new. The fixed-irradiance optical-depth optimum does not imply a global sign-count theorem for its weighted Jensen difference. value.rationale: This is a motivated complete classification of when replacing fixed mean surface illumination by a two-level light regime changes exact modeled depth-mean photosynthesis. The precise invariant (a unique optical-depth cutoff or its absence) addresses sign ambiguity in averaged phytoplankton productivity; the two-point experimental light regimes occur in the primary literature. It gives an exact duty-fraction decision boundary and high-light and near-onset scales rather than a single Jensen approximation. Biological utility is strictly conditional on a frozen instantaneous Steele response, not a field prediction.
